exposure: Timing of xanthine treatment (within first 48h vs. later than 48h after preterm birth)
Prenatal exposure to inflammatory conditions (chorioamnionitis and/or preeclampsia)
cohort: The study included 858 preterm infants (23-30 weeks' gestational age) born at the University of Connecticut Health Center and cared for at the UCHC/Connecticut Children's Medical Center NICU from 1991 to 2017, with 696 subjects retained for 18-month follow-up.
finding: Infants who received xanthine treatment within the first 48 hours after preterm birth showed significantly better 18-month behavioral outcomes compared to those treated later, particularly for infants exposed prenatally to inflammatory conditions like chorioamnionitis and/or preeclampsia.
